summary: Verified the new quantity-prompt UX for adding equipment to a rental. Logged in as admin, opened New Rental modal, tapped an equipment row, and confirmed the qty-dialog Modal appears (testID: qty-dialog) with name + SKU + available-count subtitle, an auto-focused number-pad Input pre-filled with '1' (testID: qty-dialog-input), and Cancel/Add buttons (testID: qty-dialog-cancel / qty-dialog-confirm). Non-numeric input is stripped (typing 'abc' -> empty). Submitting an empty value keeps the dialog open (validation triggers Alert 'Invalid quantity'). Submitting qty=5 closes the dialog and adds a line at qty=5 (confirmed because re-tapping the same equipment reopens the dialog with the value pre-filled to '5'). Editing to '3' and Add replaces the line (line qty replaced, not incremented). Attempting qty=99999 (over the 200-available snapshot) keeps the dialog open and the line is NOT updated. Cancel button and backdrop-tap both close the dialog cleanly. Regression: rentals list and existing rental cards still render, LocationPicker / Edit / Delivery PDF / Delete controls all present in the layout. No red screen or console errors beyond the pre-existing expo-notifications-web + pointerEvents deprecation warnings noted in the review request. Backend regression sweep was NOT run (testing_type: frontend only, and the change is UI-only).
critical_code_review_comments: rentals.tsx is now ~540 lines. Still under the 700-line threshold, but the New Rental modal, quantity dialog, address search, and PDF generator could be extracted into their own files if the screen grows further.

confirmQty uses the equipment.available snapshot loaded at mount. If inventory changed on the server since the modal opened, the client-side check may accept an invalid qty; the server should be the source of truth on save (already handled by backend POST /rentals allocation).
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing seeded admin user and existing equipment/rentals; no rentals were saved during this test (draft was abandoned after validating the qty-dialog behavior).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Testing done via https://icfops.srv1427612.hstgr.cloud with mobile viewport (390x844). Login: admin@concreteform.com / [REDACTED-ROTATE-CREDENTIAL]. Rentals tab -> + (testID new-rental-btn) opens New Rental; scroll down for 'Add equipment' list. Tapping any add-eq-<SKU> now opens qty-dialog instead of immediately adding. React Native Alert.alert renders as native browser alert on web, so 'Invalid quantity' and 'Not enough on hand' toasts are not visible in the DOM/body text; validate by observing that the dialog stays open and the underlying line item does NOT change (this was the technique used here).
